prompt: Build a BoundedCache class that holds at most N entries: inserting a new key beyond capacity evicts the oldest inserted entry, while updating an existing key just replaces its value.
explanation: LinkedHashMap iterates its keys in insertion order, so the first key its iterator yields is always the oldest inserted entry -- exactly the one a FIFO cache evicts. Eviction must happen only when the incoming key is genuinely new, which is why put checks containsKey before comparing size to capacity; re-putting an existing key keeps its original position in a LinkedHashMap. This insert-order eviction is the simpler cousin of an LRU cache, which LinkedHashMap can also build via its access-order constructor.
hints: Store the entries in a LinkedHashMap<String, String> field and the capacity in an int field set by the constructor.
In put, evict only when the key is NOT already present and size() has reached capacity.
entries.keySet().iterator().next() gives the oldest inserted key -- remove it, then put the new pair.
